signals.title: Why Large Language Models and Humans Converge and Diverge in Evaluating Creativity
signals.summary: Despite the growing use of large language models (LLMs) as creativity evaluators, evidence of their alignment with human evaluations remains mixed, raising the question of when and why their judgments converge with or diverge from human judgments. Across three studies and six widely used LLMs, we addressed this gap by identifying the standards underlying LLM creativity evaluation and examining their downstream implications.

signals.long_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly utilized to assess creativity, yet research indicates that their evaluations often do not align with those of humans. This discrepancy prompts an investigation into the conditions that lead to convergence or divergence between LLMs and human assessments. The study comprises three investigations involving six prominent LLMs, aiming to uncover the principles that guide LLMs in their creativity evaluations and the effects of these principles on outcomes. Understanding these dynamics may help refine how creativity is quantified, thereby enhancing the interplay between AI and human evaluators. Staying informed on these evaluations is vital for the community as it highlights the complexities in AI's role in creative fields and its implications for future governance in AI assessment.

signals.title: Analysing Self-Harm Representations in Language Models: a Cross-Architecture Study
signals.summary: Self-harm content is particularly challenging to detect using NLP techniques, and is also a high-stakes task which requires the highest accuracy to enable timely intervention or flagging at-risk users. We therefore present an analysis of how LLMs represent such self-harm content, which has downstream applications in self-harm detection, LLM intervention and governance and policing.

signals.long_summary: The study analyzes how large language models (LLMs) represent self-harm content, noting that detecting such content is challenging for natural language processing (NLP) techniques. The authors emphasize the importance of accurate detection, as it is crucial for timely interventions and for identifying at-risk users. The findings have significant implications for improving self-harm detection, facilitating LLM interventions, and informing governance and policy approaches to handle sensitive content effectively. signals.title: Nous Research's NousCoder-14B is an open-source coding model landing right in the Claude Code moment
signals.summary: Nous Research , the open-source artificial intelligence startup backed by crypto venture firm Paradigm , released a new competitive programming model on Monday that it says matches or exceeds several larger proprietary systems — trained in just four days using 48 of Nvidia's latest B200 graphics processors .
